chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from al-‘Amrakī ibn ‘Alī, from Yaḥyā – who was in the service of Imam Abī Ja‘far the Second (peace be upon him) – from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Bashīr al-Dahhān, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), while he was staying in al-Ḥīrah, with a group of Shī‘ah around him. He turned his face toward me and said, 'O Bashīr! Did you perform Ḥajj this year?' I replied, 'May I be sacrificed for you! No, but instead I spent ‘Arafah at the Grave – the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him).' He said, 'O Bashīr! By Allah, you did not miss anything of what was for the people of Makkah in Makkah.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! ‘Arafah is (only) in Makkah, so explain this to me.' He said, 'O Bashīr! Verily, a man from you performs Ghusl on the shore of the Euphrates, then comes to the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), knowing his rights. Allah will give him, for every foot he raises or places, one hundred accepted Ḥajj, and with them one hundred purified ‘Umrah, and one hundred battles with a sent Messenger [against the most hostile enemy of his], against the enemies of Allah and the enemies of the Messenger, and he mentioned the hadith.'

key_terms.الْحِيرَة: Al-Hīrah, a city in Iraq where Imam al-Ṣādiq stayed
key_terms.عَرَفْتُ بِالْقَبْرِ: Spent ‘Arafah at the Grave (referring to the grave of Imam al-Ḥusayn)
key_terms.قَبْرُ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing Ziyarah to Imam Husain (a.s.) instead of Hajj in Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the concept of 'Minor Hajj' (*Hajj al-Asghar*), where the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) in Karbala serves as a spiritual substitute for Mount Arafat, the pivotal station of Hajj. Ibn Qulawayh highlights the theological significance of *Ma'rifah* (gnostic knowledge of the Imam's rights) combined with ritual purity from the Euphrates, elevating the Ziyarah to a merit-equivalent of multiple accepted pilgrimages and battles with the Prophets. This underscores the Shia view of the Ahl al-Bayt as the spiritual axis connecting earthly devotion to divine acceptance.
